title: Symmetric functions as sums of thresholds
statement: Let $f$ be a function from the $n$-dimensional sign cube to $\\{−1,1\\}$ that is invariant under every permutation of its input coordinates. Then there are an integer $t\\le 2n$, a real constant $c$, and $t$ linear threshold functions $g_1,\\ldots,g_t$ on the same cube such that, for every input $x$, the real-valued version of $f$ satisfies $f(x)=c+\\sum_{j=1}^t g_j(x)$, where each $g_j(x)$ is interpreted as its real sign value.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps the sign cube of dimension $n$ to $\\{−1,1\\}$
$f$ is invariant under every permutation of its input coordinates
